name: com.satsdns/satsdns
title: SatsDNS
description: DNS hosting, secondary and dynamic DNS, domains, paid per call in sats; optional Nostr accounts.

tools.name: info
tools.description: Free: prices in sats per product and period, nameservers, limits, record types, accepted Cashu mints, how paying works, and the steps to host a zone.

tools.name: check
tools.description: Free: runs the checks a paid call runs before payment (name rules, availability, delegation, limits) without creating an invoice, and returns the price. For zone_create and secondary_create of a new zone it answers delegation_missing with the zone's own nameserver pair (expected_ns) and an ns_ticket: set exactly those NS records at the domain's registrar, wait until the registry publishes them, then call again with ns_ticket. This opens a nameserver offer (limited per caller), so it is not read-only.

tool.description: The paid tool you intend to call.

arguments.description: The arguments you would pass to that tool (payment arguments are ignored).

tools.name: domain_check
tools.description: Free: whether a domain name is available and its price in sats (offered TLDs and live 1-year prices per TLD: info, domains.tlds and domains.prices). Tightly rate-limited. If the answer carries a registry notice (tld_notice), show it to your user before they pay.

domain.description: A name under an offered TLD (info: domains.tlds), e.g. example.com.

tools.name: zone_create
tools.description: Creates a hosted, DNSSEC-signed zone on our nameservers. First call check (tool zone_create): a new zone gets its own nameserver pair, which must be set at the registrar before the payment step; pass the ns_ticket from that answer. The answer gives the zone token once (keep it: it manages the zone), the nameservers and the DS record. Paid, no account. Without payment the call returns payment_required with the price, a Lightning invoice and a Cashu payment request; pay only within what your user allowed, then call again with the same arguments plus l402='<macaroon>:<preimage>', or call with cashu='<token>'. Every request is checked for free before an invoice is made; use check first.

zone.description: The domain to host, e.g. example.com (a name you registered at any registrar).

period.description: 30d (30 days) or 1y (365 days). Prices differ: see the tool title.

ns_ticket.description: The ns_ticket from the delegation_missing answer of an earlier check or call (secret, shown once, 48 h): proves you got this zone's nameserver pair.

previous_token.description: The old zone token, only when hosting again a zone you removed or let expire (reserved for you for a while).

l402.description: Lightning payment proof for a retry: '<macaroon>:<preimage>', where macaroon comes from the payment_required answer of the previous call and preimage is the 64-hex proof your wallet returns after paying its invoice. Use it with the same tool and arguments.

cashu.description: Cashu token (cashuA... or cashuB...) worth at least the price, from an accepted mint (see info). Pays without a previous call.

tools.name: secondary_create
tools.description: We serve your zone as secondaries, transferred from your primaries (public IPv4) with a TSIG key that the answer gives once. The same nameserver-pair step as zone_create applies (check first). Paid, no account. Without payment the call returns payment_required with the price, a Lightning invoice and a Cashu payment request; pay only within what your user allowed, then call again with the same arguments plus l402='<macaroon>:<preimage>', or call with cashu='<token>'. Every request is checked for free before an invoice is made; use check first.

zone.description: The domain to host, e.g. example.com (a name you registered at any registrar).

primaries.description: Public IPv4 addresses of your primary servers (AXFR source, NOTIFY sender).

period.description: 30d (30 days) or 1y (365 days). Prices differ: see the tool title.

tools.name: hostname_create
tools.description: Creates a dynamic hostname such as myhome.dynkite.com. The answer gives the hostname token once (keep it: hostname_update and routers use it). Nothing renews it automatically: give npub to get Nostr reminders before it expires. From 2026-11-10, a create for a hostname that is already taken (bought more than a day ago) RENEWS it instead, like the renew tool: payment_required says so first, and it gives no hostname and no token. Paid, no account. Without payment the call returns payment_required with the price, a Lightning invoice and a Cashu payment request; pay only within what your user allowed, then call again with the same arguments plus l402='<macaroon>:<preimage>', or call with cashu='<token>'. Every request is checked for free before an invoice is made; use check first.

hostname.description: A label such as myhome (becomes myhome.dynkite.com), or the full name.

period.description: 30d (30 days) or 1y (365 days). Prices differ: see the tool title.

npub.description: Optional: a Nostr public key (npub1... or 64 hex) that gets direct-message reminders before the hostname expires, when grace starts and before removal. Reminders only: the key gets no control; managing the hostname still needs its token.

token.description: Only if you already hold this hostname's token (jdh_...): a create for your own hostname then answers hostname_owned with its expiry and how to renew, instead of hostname_taken (from 2026-11-10: a renewal invoice that says the hostname is already yours).

Every request is checked for free before an invoice is made; use check first.

name.description: The hosted zone (example.com) or the dynamic hostname (myhome.dynkite.com).

token.description: The zone token (jdz_...); or give api_key.

tools.name: records_change
tools.description: Free: applies up to 100 rrset changes at once, all or none. Each item REPLACEs one rrset (name and type) with the given records, or DELETEs it. Deleting records can take a site or mail offline: change only what your user asked for. Pass the zone token (jdz_...) from the create answer, or a scoped account API key (jdk_...) made in the dashboard. Either passes through your model context and transcript: treat it like a password.

token.description: The zone token (jdz_...); or give api_key.

api_key.description: Instead of token: an account API key (jdk_...) whose scope covers this object (read, or write for changes).

name.description: Owner: '@' for the apex, a relative name (www) or an absolute one.

type.description: Record type, e.g. A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, CAA, SRV, HTTPS.

ttl.description: TTL in seconds (REPLACE only; see info for the range).

changetype.description: REPLACE sets the whole rrset to records; DELETE removes the rrset.

records.description: Record contents in zone-file form (REPLACE only), e.g. "192.0.2.10" or "10 mail.example.com.".

wait.description: Optional: answer only once both nameservers (ns1 and ns2) serve the change, at most 20 s. The answer's served object says which do; use it before asking an ACME server to check a DNS-01 TXT record.

Give explicit public addresses: the caller's own address ('auto') is not available here, because through MCP it would be your client's server, not your machine (routers use /nic/update). Pass the hostname token (jdh_...) from the create answer, or a scoped account API key (jdk_...) made in the dashboard. Either passes through your model context and transcript: treat it like a password.

tools.name: account_objects
tools.description: Free, read-only: the account's state and limits, or the zones, hostnames or invoices it owns. With api_key, only the objects the key's scope covers and only their invoices (the account view of limits and counts is the same for every key). Called without nip98 it returns signature_required: the exact URL, method and body to sign, the body's sha256 and an unsigned kind 27235 event template (with proof of work for accounts without a paid order). Sign that, then call again with the same arguments plus nip98. Each signed event works once, within 60 s. Secrets that are ours to receive: object tokens, account API keys (jdk_), signed NIP-98 events; never a private key (nsec or 64 hex characters), wallet connection string or seed words. A raw hex key or seed words inside a sentence cannot be caught here.

type.description: account: state, tier, limits and whether proof of work is needed; zones, hostnames, domains: what the account owns; invoices: the 50 newest.

api_key.description: A scoped account API key (jdk_...) made in the dashboard. It passes through your model context and transcript: treat it like a password. Key model: a key reads (or, with write access, changes) only the objects in its scope, and sees only their invoices; every key reads the account view (limits and counts); a key never orders new objects and never receives a new object's shown-once token.

nip98.description: The signed NIP-98 event (base64 of its JSON) for exactly the request the signature_required answer of the same call named. Sign it with your own Nostr signer (local key, NIP-46 bunker or a signer tool); never send the private key itself, in any form (nsec, hex or seed words).

tools.name: account_order
tools.description: Orders a product into your account, paid by its own invoice: Lightning (15 min) or a new on-chain address (orders of 5,000 sats and up). Prices as in info. pay=check runs the free checks only and makes no invoice: use it first. Refused orders make no invoice. New objects need nip98; renewals and extra queries also work with an api_key whose scope covers the object. Pay only within what your user allowed, then poll order_status with the invoice id. Accounts without a paid order are limited (see info, accounts.npub_limits). Called without nip98 it returns signature_required: the exact URL, method and body to sign, the body's sha256 and an unsigned kind 27235 event template (with proof of work for accounts without a paid order). Sign that, then call again with the same arguments plus nip98. Each signed event works once, within 60 s. Secrets that are ours to receive: object tokens, account API keys (jdk_), signed NIP-98 events; never a private key (nsec or 64 hex characters), wallet connection string or seed words. A raw hex key or seed words inside a sentence cannot be caught here.

tools.name: claim
tools.description: Free: puts a zone, hostname or domain bought with a token into your Nostr account, so you get expiry reminders by DM and can manage it with API keys. If another account owns a zone or hostname, a 72-hour recovery starts instead and that owner is told. A domain takes its hosted zone along when no account owns that zone; a domain another account owns answers domain_owned (its owner releases it first; no recovery). Called without nip98 it returns signature_required: the exact URL, method and body to sign, the body's sha256 and an unsigned kind 27235 event template (with proof of work for accounts without a paid order). Sign that, then call again with the same arguments plus nip98. Each signed event works once, within 60 s. Secrets that are ours to receive: object tokens, account API keys (jdk_), signed NIP-98 events; never a private key (nsec or 64 hex characters), wallet connection string or seed words. A raw hex key or seed words inside a sentence cannot be caught here. The signature_required answer shows the body with the token masked; its sha256 covers the real token.

tools.name: domain_register
tools.description: Registers a domain for the registrant your user names. The answer gives the domain token (jdd_...) that manages it: Keep the domain token (jdd_) secret, and keep the payment proof you used (the l402 value or the cashu token): calling again with the same arguments and proof within 24 h shows the same token, and domain_token_recover with the proof replaces a lost token at any time. Paid, no account: without payment it answers payment_required with this order's price (valid 15 minutes), a Lightning invoice (L402) and a Cashu request, after every free check passed (no invoice otherwise). Pay only within what your user allowed, then call again with exactly the same arguments plus l402='<macaroon>:<preimage>' or cashu='<token>' (a Cashu token is melted into the service's Lightning wallet at once; if the mint does not pay, the token stays yours). Free quote first: domain_check.

domain.description: The domain, e.g. example.com (an offered TLD: info, domains.tlds).

registrant.description: The registrant of record: the real person or organization your user is, never you and never placeholders. Required: name, email (must accept mail: the registrar asks to confirm it within 15 days), phone (+CC.NUMBER, e.g. +1.6045551234), address1, city, postal_code, country (ISO 3166 two letters). Optional: organization, address2, state.

attestation.description: true only after your user confirmed: 'I am authorised by the named registrant to register this domain for them, and the registrant accepts the registration agreement' (https://satsdns.com/registration-agreement).

nameservers.description: Your own nameservers (2-13 host names); leave out to use ours.

host_zone.description: Also host the zone here for a year (the hosting add-on); the answer then has a zone token (jdz_) too.

owner_npub.description: Optional Nostr key (npub1... or 64 hex) whose account owns the domain from payment on and gets expiry reminders. Without it the domain token alone manages the domain.

l402.description: Lightning payment proof for a retry: '<macaroon>:<preimage>', where macaroon comes from the payment_required answer of the previous call and preimage is the 64-hex proof your wallet returns after paying its invoice. Use it with the same tool and arguments.

cashu.description: Cashu token (cashuA... or cashuB...) worth at least the price, from an accepted mint (see info). Pays without a previous call.

tools.name: domain_transfer
tools.description: Transfers a domain from another registrar (adds a year). The current registrar may take 5-7 days; domain_status shows progress. Keep the domain token (jdd_) secret, and keep the payment proof you used (the l402 value or the cashu token): calling again with the same arguments and proof within 24 h shows the same token, and domain_token_recover with the proof replaces a lost token at any time. Paid, no account: without payment it answers payment_required with this order's price (valid 15 minutes), a Lightning invoice (L402) and a Cashu request, after every free check passed (no invoice otherwise). Pay only within what your user allowed, then call again with exactly the same arguments plus l402='<macaroon>:<preimage>' or cashu='<token>' (a Cashu token is melted into the service's Lightning wallet at once; if the mint does not pay, the token stays yours). Free quote first: domain_check.

tools.name: domain_token_recover
tools.description: Free: replaces a lost domain token using the l402 proof or cashu token the domain's registration or transfer was paid with. The old token stops working. Works while the domain is registered here, unless an account owns it (its owner uses token_rotate) or the registrant changed since.

tools.name: domain_token_email
tools.description: Free: without code, sends a one-time code to the registrant email of a domain no account owns (the answer is the same whether or not it qualifies); with code, replaces the domain token. The code works once, for 60 minutes. Ask your user for the code; never guess it.

domain.description: The domain, e.g. example.com (an offered TLD: info, domains.tlds).

code.description: Leave out to send a one-time code to the registrant email; then call again with the code from that mail.

tools.name: domain_refund
tools.description: Free: claims the refund of a domain order made without an account that failed after payment, with its payment proof (l402 or cashu), within 30 days. Checked at once; paid by hand over Lightning to destination. Completed orders are final.

destination.description: Your Lightning address (name@host) or an LNURL for the refund.
